gaps.sentence: She ___ three chapters so far this week.
gaps.hint: so far this week counts to now
gaps.explanation: 'So far' measures up to the present, so the present perfect is needed: has written.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me yesterday to say she had arrived safely.
gaps.hint: yesterday fixes a finished past action
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so the past simple is used: phoned.

gaps.sentence: When I came downstairs, the whole house ___ of fresh bread.
gaps.hint: smell as a state verb in past
gaps.explanation: 'Smell' as a state verb takes simple tenses, here the past simple: smelled.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her keys again — this is the third time this month!
gaps.hint: third time this month connects to now
gaps.explanation: 'This is the third time' links a recent event to now, so the present perfect is required: has lost.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to contact him all week, but his phone is always engaged.
gaps.hint: all week repeated attempts until now
gaps.explanation: Repeated attempts continuing up to now take the present perfect continuous: have been trying.

gaps.sentence: He ___ the same bus to work every morning, even in winter.
gaps.hint: every morning signals a fixed routine
gaps.explanation: 'Every morning' describes a fixed routine, which takes the present simple: catches.

gaps.sentence: I usually walk to work, but today I ___ the bus because it is raining.
gaps.hint: today contrasts with the usual habit
gaps.explanation: 'But today' signals a temporary break from habit, so the present continuous is correct: am taking.

gaps.sentence: The taxi ___ as soon as you come out of the terminal — look for a blue shirt.
gaps.hint: in progress at the future arrival moment
gaps.explanation: An action that will be in progress at a future moment takes the future continuous: will be waiting.
